CONCLUDED 2026-06-17 (not viable in current scene). In-tick spatial diagnostic (diff burst frames → motion centroid, 70 labeled detections w/ frames on disk: 18 real-animal incl wrong_species, 52 FP). FP and animal motion centroids are spatially ENTANGLED — both center-weighted (median ~0.5/0.5). NO edge band removes FP without removing a comparable-or-greater share of animals: left15% catches 8%FP vs 17%animals (hurts animals MORE), right15% 12%FP vs 11%animals (wash), top15% 10%FP vs 11%animals (wash), bottom15% 0 animals but only 1/52 FP (negligible). No zero-observed-FN ROI exists → FN-veto stands on data, not assumption. Reinforces exp #4 (motion knobs don't separate FP from animal) + exp #1 (notification-layer REVIEW prefix is the right architecture, not trigger-side suppression). See JOURNAL 2026-06-17.

CONCLUDED 2026-07-07 (shipped). The sharpness floor (min_sharpness_threshold=11.0) in _capture_and_select_best_frame silently discarded low-light/dusk captures (return None,None before DB logging or notification), causing unrecorded false negatives — e.g. the 07-07 ~19:10 pond bird detected 17x across 4 captured bursts, never logged. Shipped on branch fix/human-gate-blur-gate. See runs/0005 + JOURNAL 2026-07-08.

ROLLED BACK 2026-07-09 (same day as ship). AE=short was meant to raise dusk sharpness_score above the 11.0 floor. Measurement on saved frames shows it CANNOT: sharpness_score is Laplacian variance, which scales with frame contrast/brightness; AE=short lowers luma by construction (19h matched-hour: luma 68.9->52.0), so it pushes MORE bursts below the floor, not fewer. Run 0006's own pre-registered 'midday regression => reconsider' trigger also fired (16h lap 19.18->15.07). FN unmeasured + plausible FN rise via the below-floor+no-animal mute path => FN-veto => reverted to AE=normal. Reopened as running to collect the matched-hour 17-19h AE=normal baseline that was never captured. CONCLUDED 2026-07-10: AE=normal dusk baseline now in (07-10 17-18h sharpness 6.9-9.4) and is indistinguishable from AE=short (07-09 17-18h 7.8-8.6) — both below the 11.0 floor. AE mode is not the lever; the floor statistic is (backlog id 8, now active). AE=normal retained. See runs/0006.

CONCLUDED 2026-07-21 (KEEP, live). ROOT CAUSE behind exp #6/#5: min_sharpness_threshold=11.0 on raw Laplacian variance is a SCENE-BRIGHTNESS gate, not a blur gate (P(lap<11.0)=0% luma>=80, 71% luma 60-80, 100% luma<40 over 470 frames), so at dusk the blur-gate mute path fires as a function of darkness. Fix (c/b hybrid) SHIPPED 2026-07-18 commit 683f5f3: blur_mute_min_luma=70.0 — below-floor no-animal review-class bursts are only muted when luma>=70; when luma<70 (genuinely dark) they flow to REVIEW instead of being silently muted, closing the unobservable-dusk-FN class. Validated over two dusk-heavy nights (07-20, 07-21), both FN-veto CLEAN (0 concealed animals across 14 adjudicated review-class muted/un-muted frames). 07-21 volume bump quantified: 9/12 below-floor no-animal dusk frames luma<70 -> un-muted to REVIEW (all true-negative empty scenes), 3 muted; ~9 extra REVIEW msgs/dusk-night, no guardrail trip. 0 MAIN leaks; dusk birds (incl. below-floor 2749) correctly routed to MAIN. Rollback = git revert 683f5f3 + restart, or raise the knob. See runs/0007.

ACTIVATED + SHIPPED 2026-07-27 (commit 50aa451, restart-gated 07-28T03:25), running/live. Fourth human-gate leak path: MegaDetector finds NO person box on extreme close-up / motion-blurred PARTIAL human bodies (pc 0.02-0.15, detection_count 0), the ensemble says no_animal and raw top-1 is NULL, so all three existing triggers are blind and the person's photo is sent as a REVIEW notification (3 confirmed on 07-27: ids 3544, 3553, 3554 — note 2 of the 3 were human-labelled false_positive, so the label stream understates this leak). Fix: mute (Telegram only; still species-ID'd + DB-logged with new human_proximity_muted column) review-class bursts landing within human_proximity_window_seconds (120, env PERFORMANCE_HUMAN_PROXIMITY_WINDOW_SECONDS, BOUNDS [0,600], 0=off) of the last HUMAN-status detection. Precedence: Human > Human-Proximity > Blur > Scene > Sampling. FN-veto cleared BY MEASUREMENT, not assumption: 0 of the 12 human-labelled animal/animal_wrong_id review-class rows since the human gate went live (2026-07-08) fall within 120s of a preceding human burst; nearest is 329s (2.7x margin), while the 3 leaks sit at 76-108s. Cost 118/902 = 13% of review-class bursts since 07-08. 474 tests pass. Nightly duty: adjudicate every human_proximity_muted=1 burst. Rollback: window=0 + restart. See runs/0010.

CANDIDATE, not shipped (2026-07-29, see runs/0010 night-2 observations). The human-proximity gate is causal/backward-looking, so the LEADING EDGE of a human visit can never be muted: 3829 (15:32:34, sent to REVIEW) carries a close-range motion smear 75 s BEFORE the visit's first HUMAN-status burst (3830), with the previous human burst 1909 s earlier and trailing density 0. No in-bounds window or density threshold reaches it. The only mechanism shape that would: defer the Telegram send of a review-class burst by ~120 s and cancel it if a HUMAN-status detection lands in the meantime (a small async hold buffer in notification dispatch, fail-open = send on any error). Parked because the single observed instance is an UNRECOGNISABLE blur smear (no face/body part/individual), i.e. no privacy harm to respond to, and it would add latency to every REVIEW alert. Promote if a RECOGNISABLE person photo is sent on the leading edge of a visit (before the first HUMAN burst). RECURRENCE 2026-07-30 (night 3): second instance, 3867 at 15:22:03 sent to REVIEW with a dark/blue edge smear 51 s before the visit's first HUMAN burst (3868); previous human ~7.5 h earlier, density 0, so again unreachable by any backward-looking rule. Also adjudicated NOT recognisable -> criterion still unmet, stays parked. Rate so far: 2 instances in 2 nights (~once per human-visit day) -- recurrence of a harmless smear is not grounds for adding ~120 s latency to every REVIEW alert; only recognisability promotes this.

nightly_verdict: Quiet day, 47 triggers, and the new person filter proved its worth: a close-up photo of someone in the garden was held back only because the camera had seen people repeatedly that half-hour -- the older rule would have sent it to you. Nothing was hidden that shouldn't be, no animals missed, and the one bird tonight (a crow at dusk, almost too dark to see) still reached you.
